svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.9.9.3 Shared Egress Facilities
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.9 MEANS OF EGRESS
Shared Egress Facilities

g.text: An exit stairway serving more than one suite
A public corridor serving more than one suite,
An exterior passageway: more than one suite,
A balcony: more than one suite,
In each case, the dwelling unit needs a second and separate means of egress (Sentence (1)).

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
A dwelling unit has a second and separate means of
egress where its egress door opens onto
(a) an exit stairway serving more than one suite, (b) a
public corridor serving more than one suite and served
by a single exit, (c) an exterior passageway serving
more than one suite, served by a single exit stairway or
ramp, and more than 1.5 m (4′-11″) above adjacent ground
level, or (d) a balcony with the same three conditions
as (c). Except as provided in Sentences (2) and (3).
In a house with a secondary suite, an upper dwelling
unit above another dwelling unit or common space has
a second and separate means of egress where its
egress door opens onto an exterior passageway that
(a) has a floor assembly with a fire-resistance rating
less than 45 min, (b) is served by a single exit
stairway or ramp, and (c) is more than 1.5 m above
adjacent ground level.
In a house with a secondary suite, where either
egress door opens onto a shared egress facility
served by a single exit stairway or ramp (other than
Sentence (2)), a second means of egress is not
needed
If the building is sprinklered, or if the dwelling units
have separate and direct access from each storey to (a)
a balcony, or (b) an openable window conforming to
Clauses 9.9.9.1.(2)(a) and (b).
Drawn: the four shared egress facilities of Sentence (1). Walls cut low in (a) and (b). Not to scale.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.9.9.3. (page 9-55)
